title: The Nausea of Touch
description: Rendered in oil on canvas, The Nausea of Touch is a deeply conceptual piece born from an intersection of existential philosophy, high-fashion subversion, and the visceral anxiety of romantic experience. The artwork draws its core inspiration from Jean-Paul Sartre’s seminal diary novel Nausea, translating philosophical dread into a tangible, bodily sensation. Visually, the composition references a striking runway detail by Bottega Veneta, where models carried water inside condoms over their hands. While the original fashion statement carried ecological undertones, I subvert and reshape this imagery into a double-edged metaphor for modern love. The liquid-filled, restrictive membranes trapping the hands become a visual manifestation of emotional suffocation. It explores the profound, existential nausea that can accompany intimacy - where the very tools of human connection and touch become heavy, paralyzed, and weighted down by the anxiety of loving another.
